direct_answer:
Yes. MOL Group discloses that it has a climate change mitigation transition plan (disclosed for the first time in the 2024 sustainability statement) that was approved by the Sustainable Development Committee of the Board in February 2025, by the Board of Directors in March 2025, and by the AGM in April 2025 [Source 3].

However, based on the disclosed information, the transition plan is not demonstrated as aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C. MOL states that assessing compatibility with a 1.5°C pathway is difficult and that an oil & gas industry-specific benchmark for a 1.5°C compatible gross absolute GHG pathway is “not yet available”; it will assess the feasibility of adopting such a plan once relevant guidelines/resources (primarily from SBTi) become available [Source 1]. MOL also notes its 2030 targets are below the SBTi cross-sector pathway (which it cites as 42% gross Scope 1, 2 and 3 reduction by 2030 from 2020 levels) [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: Evidence shows MOL has a transition plan and provides governance approvals and key targets/milestones (2030/2050) [Source 3]. But the disclosures do not provide a clear explanation that the plan/targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C; instead, MOL highlights the lack of an industry-specific 1.5°C benchmark and indicates it will assess feasibility later when SBTi guidance becomes available, and it acknowledges its 2030 targets are below the cited SBTi cross-sector pathway [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit explanation of how MOL’s transition plan and GHG targets are compatible with limiting global warming to 1.5°C (as required by ESRS E1-1.16(a)); current disclosure emphasizes difficulty and lack of benchmark rather than demonstrating alignment [Source 1].

Whether and how MOL’s GHG targets are science-based and compatible with 1.5°C, including the framework/methodology used, underlying climate/policy scenarios for target-setting, and whether targets have been externally assured (ESRS E1-4.34(e)); the passages cite scenarios used for forecasts and mention SBTi, but do not confirm science-based/1.5°C-compatible targets or external assurance [Source 1].
Clear statement of 1.5°C alignment status (aligned/not aligned) for the transition plan; the passages do not provide a definitive alignment claim [Source 1].
key_findings: MOL Group has a disclosed climate transition plan, approved in 2025 (Sustainable Development Committee in Feb 2025; Board in Mar 2025; AGM in Apr 2025) [Source 3].

The plan includes 2030 and 2050 milestones/targets, including: -25% absolute gross Scope 1 and 2 by 2030 vs 2019; -5% absolute gross Scope 3 use-phase (Category 11) by 2030 vs 2022; net zero on all scopes by 2050; and 30–40% of CAPEX allocated to low-carbon/sustainable projects (2025–2030) [Source 3].

MOL indicates challenges in assessing 1.5°C compatibility and notes the absence of a widely accepted oil & gas-specific 1.5°C benchmark; it will assess feasibility of adopting such a plan when SBTi guidelines/resources become available [Source 1].

MOL states its 2030 targets are below the SBTi cross-sector pathway it cites (42% reduction by 2030 from 2020 levels for gross Scope 1, 2 and 3) and notes it is excluded from EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks [Source 1].
